title: Pineapple Gazpacho (Chilled Pineapple and Vegetable Soup)
description: A refreshing chilled Continental soup made with fresh pineapple, vegetables, olive oil, and citrus. Served cold with elegant fine-dining garnishes for a bright and tropical appetizer.

ingredients.title: Gazpacho Base
items: Fresh ripe pineapple – 500 g (core removed, chopped)
Extra virgin olive oil – 40 ml (cold-pressed, fruity profile)
Rice vinegar or white wine vinegar – 15 ml
Ice cubes – a few, to chill during blending

ingredients.title: For the Garnish (Fine-Dining Presentation)
items: Micro herbs – a mix of basil, coriander, and red amaranth
Red chili – finely sliced (optional, for contrast)
Olive oil pearls or basil oil – for finish

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Base
steps: In a blender, combine pineapple, yellow bell pepper, cucumber, celery, shallot, ginger, and garlic.
Add lime juice, vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Blend until completely smooth — about 2–3 minutes on high speed.
Add ice cubes while blending to maintain a bright, fresh color and prevent oxidation.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Refine the Texture
steps: Pass the mixture through a fine chinois or muslin cloth to achieve a silky, velvety texture.
Adjust seasoning — balance sweetness, acidity, and salinity carefully.
Aim for a bright, tropical acidity with subtle vegetal depth.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Chill
steps: Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
Serve at 4–6°C for best mouthfeel and aromatic expression.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Plating (Restaurant-Style Presentation)
steps: Pour the chilled gazpacho into a pre-chilled glass bowl or white rimmed plate.
Arrange pineapple and cucumber brunoise at the center.
Add pickled shallot rings and a few micro herbs.
Drizzle with basil oil or place a few olive oil pearls.
Garnish with edible flowers for color contrast.
Optional fine-dining touch: serve with a compressed pineapple cube (vacuum-sealed with lime zest and a hint of chili) or a parmesan tuille on the side for texture.

servingSuggestions.title: Wine Pairing
items: A chilled Sauvignon Blanc complements the tropical and vegetal notes.
Serve well chilled as an appetizer or amuse-bouche.

chefTips: Flavor balance: The key is harmony between pineapple sweetness, cucumber freshness, and citrus-lime acidity.
Add ice cubes while blending to maintain a bright, fresh color and prevent oxidation.
Pass the gazpacho through a fine chinois for a silky, restaurant-quality texture.
Gazpacho base can be stored refrigerated (airtight) for up to 48 hours; stir before serving.
